about: The smoke suite run by tools/dev/smoke.ps1. Each scenario is one hidden test run through shoot.ps1. Fields: name; about (what it checks, for the player); script (dev actions, tools/dev/README.md: times from app start, about 2 s after launch); shots (seconds after launch to capture: a beat after the last action; a shot whose window, or the scenario's window, isn't there or drawn yet waits for it, up to 10 s); settings (extra settings.json members, starting with a comma); window (also capture this window, by part of its title); desk (also capture every window where it sits); mind (point the profile at tools/dev/mock_mind.py); mindReply; mindRequests (the least the mock must be asked); expect (regexes, case-sensitive, that some log line must match); forbid (more regexes no log line may match, on top of ERROR, Exception and SCRIPT ERROR); ignore (regexes for known harmless lines); beside (first start hidden stand-ins for the player's own app, copies that aren't test runs: one holds a one-copy lock of their own, never the player's, a second must quit at once, and the scenario runs beside them). The top-level ignore applies to every scenario. Calibrate expect and ignore from real runs; never loosen forbid to make a run pass. Which run in a check (smoke.ps1 -Changed, as check.ps1 runs it): every scenario when a file matching one of all changed (shared code and the harness itself); each scenario whose covers match a changed file; and boot whenever a file matching app changed (anything the app runs). Patterns are wildcards on paths from the checkout's root, with forward slashes. READMEs never count (a character's persona.md does: the app reads it), so a change to tests or docs alone runs none; with no list of what changed (git couldn't say, or on main itself), every scenario runs.

scenarios.name: boot
scenarios.about: A fresh profile: the cabinet and the companion come up and nothing in the log goes wrong.

scenarios.name: beside
scenarios.about: A test run goes ahead beside the player's own app (a stand-in holding a one-copy lock of its own, leaving the player's free), while a second such copy still quits at once; the test copy shows no tray icon or Windows notice, never reads the talk key or the mouse, and hears silence instead of opening the microphone.
expect: ^Main: a test run, beside any other copy \(no single-instance lock\), on its own profile
^DesktopWindow: a test run: the player's mouse buttons are never read, nor their pointer followed
^Listening: a test run: the talk key is never read
^Ears: a test run never opens the microphone

scenarios.name: firstrun
scenarios.about: A new player's first run: the Welcome opens beside the cabinet.

scenarios.name: settings
scenarios.about: Every Settings page opens, and none is wider than the window (settingswidths logs any that is).

scenarios.name: chat
scenarios.about: Saying something to the companion reaches their mind (the mock), and their reply shows in their bubble.
scenarios.mindReply: Hi! It's good to see you. How did today go?
expect: ^Chat: her bubble showed its first words \d+ ms after asking, the whole reply

scenarios.name: skills
scenarios.about: Settings → Skills lists the seeded skills (one in the app's folder, one broken); a vault's skills folder linked on the page says how many skills it has and lists them (two, one with a hint); a skill's Settings › opens its own page, headed by where it is (‹ Skills › tea-timer, top left) and its name, and ‹ Skills goes back to the list where it was scrolled to, keyboard focus on the way back each time (‹ Skills going down, the skill's Settings › coming up); a skill with a name too long for the window wraps it in its page's heading, and neither its page nor the list is wider than the window (settingswidths, there); asked for one by name, the companion's mind (the mock) reads it with their skill tool, then answers.
scenarios.mindReply: Warm the pot first, then four minutes.
expect: ^Chat: her bubble showed its first words \d+ ms after asking, the whole reply
^Settings: \d+ of \d+ pages measured, below them skills \S+ keeping-the-players-weekly-reading-list-and-every-book-note-tidy$

scenarios.name: skill-folders
scenarios.about: A stand-in notes folder granted to a skill on its own page (Settings → Skills → its Settings ›); asked to add a line to a note there, the companion's mind (the mock) reads it and appends a line with their note tools, and the file shows it; Undo on the skill's page takes it out again. Asked again, then the player adds a line of their own, Undo is refused, says so beside the changes (in view), and leaves the player's line.
expect: ^Notes: today\.md ends: - A line from the mock mind\.$
^Skills: Undone: today\.md is as it was\.$
^Skills: today\.md has changed since, so it was left as it is; the version from before is still kept\.$
^Notes: today\.md ends: - The player's own line\.$

scenarios.name: skill-change
scenarios.about: Told the player now does something a skill describes differently, the companion's mind (the mock) suggests a change to that skill: the card by the stool says plainly what changes (Update how tea-timer works: the new wording, and what it was), See the change opens the exact lines, and Remember it writes only that line; the skill's own page lists the change, and Undo puts the skill back.
expect: ^Skills: she suggested a change to tea-timer: Written: from now on tea-timer's instructions say "rinse the pot with hot water first"\.$
^Skills: Undone: SKILL\.md is as it was\.$

scenarios.name: memory
scenarios.about: The memory book opens on its tabs with a few seeded notes, facts and agenda items; a fact edited is saved on leaving it, and one the companion rewords while it is being edited asks which to keep, then keeps the player's.
expect: ^Memory book: asked which to keep: \S+ changed this meanwhile, to: “Bob promised her a Medium problem.”

scenarios.name: agendacancel
scenarios.about: Asked to take something off the agenda, the companion does it in that reply: the job interview the seed put there leaves the memory book's Agenda tab.
expect: ^Chat: her bubble showed its first words \d+ ms after asking, the whole reply

scenarios.name: chathistory
scenarios.about: Chat history follows the conversation while it is open: lines said meanwhile come in at the end, what the companion had in mind for a reply stays open as more come in, and with the player scrolled up the new lines leave their place and a "New lines below" note takes them there.
scenarios.mindReply: Hi! It's good to see you. How did today go?
expect: ^Chat history: \d new lines? shown, at the end
^Chat history: \d new lines? shown, below the player's place

scenarios.name: chathistory-hidden
scenarios.about: Chat history leaves out what the app tells the companion (here a refused agenda change after each reply) and still follows the talk: a line the player says under the number of a hidden line taken back comes in, and after the chat is cleared with a line said at once, the history shows that line, not a blank window.
expect: ^Chat history: 2 new lines shown, at the end
^Chat history: 1 new line shown, at the end

scenarios.name: crt
scenarios.about: The CRT's small system opens, then its MEMOS app.

scenarios.name: agendaapp
scenarios.about: The CRT's AGENDA app follows the agenda while it is open: the job interview the seed put there leaves it when the companion takes it off, without reopening it.
expect: ^Agenda app: changed while open, now 1 ahead

scenarios.name: reminder
scenarios.about: A reminder set a few seconds ahead goes off, with its ticket.

scenarios.name: focus
scenarios.about: A focus session starts from the screen and counts down on it.

scenarios.name: memos
scenarios.about: Memos hang and pin on the cabinet's side, and the hanging one opens as a sheet.

scenarios.name: windows-above
scenarios.about: Settings and the memory book stay above the cabinet and the companion: while the cabinet rises for a moment and after it sinks back, with Always on top off, then with it on (ticked in Settings) and the cabinet rising again; then a ticket and the file dialog "Add a character…" opens are above them both.
expect: ^Windows, top first: Settings \(on top\), the cabinet \(on top\)$
^Windows, top first: What \S+ remembers \(on top\), Settings \(on top\), the cabinet \(on top\)$
^Windows, top first: Beside the Cabinet ticket \(on top\), file dialog "Add a character" \(on top\), What \S+ remembers \(on top\), Settings \(on top\), the cabinet \(on top\)$
forbid: ^Windows, top first: .+, Beside the Cabinet ticket

scenarios.name: windows-above-dialog
scenarios.about: With Always on top off, the file dialog "Add a character…" opens above Settings, and a ticket above both, while the cabinet rises for the dialog and after it sinks back.
expect: ^Windows, top first: Beside the Cabinet ticket \(on top\), file dialog "Add a character" \(on top\), Settings \(on top\), the cabinet \(on top\)$
^Windows, top first: (Beside the Cabinet ticket \(on top\), )?file dialog "Add a character", Settings, the cabinet$
forbid: ^Windows, top first: .+, Beside the Cabinet ticket
